Innodata opens a 3D motion-capture lab for robot training

The New Jersey facility uses Vicon cameras to track people, robots and objects for training data and evaluation services.

The Robot Report ↗30 September 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 2Videos 1

Capturing motion directly in 3D

Innodata has opened a New Jersey laboratory developed with Vicon for humanoid and physical-AI data. Infrared optical cameras measure three-dimensional movement directly instead of inferring it from two-dimensional footage. The company describes sub-millimeter measurement accuracy and millisecond latency.

A shared frame for people and robots

Tracking humans, robots and handled objects in the same space connects demonstrations with object positions and machine responses. Customers can buy existing datasets, commission custom capture or bring robots for evaluation under scripted scenarios. External measurements also provide a reference against a robot’s own sensor reports.

Measurement is only part of validation

The service offers developers reference data for model training and evaluation. Camera accuracy is a measurement specification, not a robot task-success rate. Real operating conditions, differences between robot bodies and failure cases still require testing beyond the laboratory before the resulting behavior can be relied upon in deployment.
